links.comparator_used: Other target reading grade levels (7-17) specified in the same Gemini transformation of radiology reports; no default no-instruction prompt arm
links.outcome: Stakeholder preference, accuracy, readability and error rates (generalizations, omissions, hallucinations) across target reading grade levels
links.effect: Preferences peaked at grade 16 and declined at grade 17, especially among laypersons; higher grades were generally preferred (range 12-17). Accuracy was the strongest predictor of preference (OR 30.29, 33.05, 2.16 for radiologists, physicians, laypersons; p<0.001), followed by readability (OR 2.73, 1.70, 2.01; p<0.001).
links.tradeoff: Lower grade levels improved readability but increased errors (generalizations, omissions, hallucinations); higher grade levels improved accuracy but sharply reduced readability. Authors note the limits of unsupervised LLM transformation.
links.quote: Lower reading grades improved readability but increased errors, while higher grades improved accuracy but reduced readability.

design_hint: reading-level constraint for LLM-simplified radiology reports
